subject: Performance clauses and stepwise pricing — private offer (AWS)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Todd <alex.todd@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance clauses and stepwise pricing — private offer (AWS)

Alex — attaching the updated MAP workbook (v3) and a DocSend link with the milestone table. Key changes highlighted: a) stepwise discount triggers tied to committed monthly run rate (CMRR) and b) an explicit performance clause that gates deeper discounts based on p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput thresholds during the evaluation period.

High-level proposal:
- 90-day evaluation window (canary + staged ramp)
- Baseline private offer: list pricing for x-large inference nodes
- Milestone 1 (30 days): 10% pre-commit credit applied after successful smoke tests and initial throughput (>= 60% of target)
- Milestone 2 (60 days): 20% discount applied when cumulative committed spend >= $75k and p99 latency <= 350ms for the critical path
- Milestone 3 (90 days): 30% discount + commitment conversion when 3-month ramp achieves target sustained throughput and SOC2 evidence provided

Please review the performance gating language on tab 'Performance & Discounts' — we added a clause that allows a 14-day cure if thresholds are missed before stepping back to list price. Also included the private-offer flow steps for AWS Marketplace procurement (Doc ID link).

Attachments: [Attachment: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]
Links: https://docsend.com/view/acme-map-v3

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the gating mechanics.

--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Alex Todd <alex.todd@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance clauses and stepwise pricing — private offer (AWS)

Sean — thanks for the doc. Quick clarifying questions from procurement and our infra team: 
1) Measurement windows — are p99 and throughput calculated over rolling 24h windows or per-deployment windows? We need deterministic measurement windows to feed into our finance triggers.
2) SOC2 — can you include a one-page SOC2 summary? Our security/compliance lead wants something concise to share with legal.
3) Discount timing — Procurement is pushing to move the Milestone 2 discount to 45 days instead of 60 and make the threshold cumulative spend a bit lower given our pilot size. Could you run a version of the MAP with a 45/90 day cadence instead of 30/60/90?

Also please confirm the Private Offer flow on AWS Marketplace — do we need to pre-configure the private offer with the baseline list rate and apply credits, or can we encode stepwise discounts so the private offer automatically adjusts?

Thanks — can we aim to have this nailed down before our commercial review on Friday?

Alex Todd
Head of Cloud Platforms, Acme Retail
alex.todd@acme-retail.com | +1 212-555-0104
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Todd <alex.todd@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance clauses and stepwise pricing — private offer (AWS)

Alex — good questions, answers below and I attached the SOC2 summary.

1) Measurement windows: We propose rolling 7-day aggregates for throughput and a rolling 24-hour p99 calculated from production traffic routed through the private offer endpoints. This gives a balance between noisy minute-level spikes and overly long monthly smoothing. We can make it a fixed UTC day window if you prefer deterministic finance cutoffs.

2) SOC2: attached as requested — ACME_SOC2-Summary.pdf (one-page summary).

3) Discount timing: We're open to compressing Milestone 2 to 45 days. Suggested compromise for pilot economics: 
- Milestone A (day 15): 5% pilot credit after canary validation (smoke tests + basic throughput)
- Milestone B (day 45): 15% discount applied once cumulative spend >= $50k and rolling-24h p99 <= 400ms
- Milestone C (day 90): 30% discount + conversion to committed private offer when 3-month ramp >= $250k ARR-equivalent (or volume equivalent), plus SOC2 evidence supplied.

Performance gating caveat: if p99 breaches but average throughput is growing, we propose a 14-day remediation window; if unresolved, discount resets to previous tier. We added explicit examples in the MAP spreadsheet so legal can map to invoice credits rather than retro billing adjustments.

AWS private-offer mechanics: AWS private offers do not support dynamic contract-driven step-downs natively. Typical pattern is:
- Create private offer at baseline (list) rate
- Apply an upfront credit or staged credit schedule that is invoiced/claimed as milestones are met (these are line-item credits tied to the agreement, not automated marketplace-rate changes)
- Our finance/legal will provide a credits schedule (DocuSign) that references the MAP milestone table and HubSpot deal id so procurement can reconcile credits against invoices.

Attachments: [Attachment: ACME_SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]
Related link: https://hubspot.company.com/deal/ACME-2489

If that approach works, we'll draft the credit schedule and legal-friendly milestone language for you and procurement. Can Jordan and Marissa loop in Legal/Finance for a one-hour review on Thursday?

--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Todd <alex.todd@acme-retail.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance clauses and stepwise pricing — private offer (AWS)

Alex / team — appreciate the rapid back-and-forth. We approve the compressed milestone cadence Sean proposed (15 / 45 / 90) for the pilot, with the following action items to keep things moving fast: 
- Redwood to produce a one-page commercial term sheet that converts the MAP milestones to a credit schedule (legal-friendly language) by EOD Monday.
- Redwood Finance to produce the AWS private-offer credit instrument and a DocuSign template referencing ACME-2489.
- Acme procurement to confirm whether they want credits applied as invoice line-item credits or a one-time settlement (we recommend invoice credits for month-to-month reconciliation).
- Product: confirm fallback model variant (lower-cost quantized model) is permitted for canary traffic; Marissa please confirm viability and expected latency delta.
- 1-hour legal/finance sync scheduled (Thu 09/23) — Jordan to share invite.

If you all are aligned on this, we'll start the HubSpot private-offer workflow and draft the Private Offer payload. Jordan — loop in Legal/SRE as needed.

Jordan Blake
